items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: You ever heard of Chuck Cecil? ... Well Chuck Cecil runs programs, the hits of ’48 and ’49 and so on.

ctx.x: What was your take on the reason the big bands really disappeared?

Well I think probably it was television for one thing, and just a lack of interest and I don’t know why really. We had all these dance halls that closed down all of a sudden. The radio, see the radio stopped. One of the big things about the big band era was the radio support. If you lived in this coast you could start about ten o’clock at night and turn on your radio and there’d be remotes from all over the world. And every band you can think of was on. And if you listened to — what the hell’s his name that does…
